formula_checks.name: grossFromNet
formula_checks.reviewer_why: A monotone federal-schedule inversion on the stated no-payroll/no-state domain; [net,3×net] brackets the 2026 rates, and50 bisections give ample numerical precision.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: All five cases agree to 1e-6; its one caller is MK-CF-F-186, whose fault is the 401(k) left out, not this inversion.

formula_checks.name: progressiveMonthlyTax
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Clipping negative income months to0 breaks the year-tax reconciliation when a legitimate loss lowers cumulative taxable income. This is an allocation illustration, not payroll withholding.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Restrict inputs to explicitly nonnegative accruals, or permit negative tax adjustments that telescope to tax on the actual annual base.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Real but latent: a loss month is clipped to $0, so the months add to the tax on $76,222.36 ($7,938.92), not the year's $63,110.93 ($5,393.31). Its one caller, buildIncomeState, also hands it no filing status or state rate (single, federal only) — the legacy reader the handoff names as MK-CF-F-049 (another part).

formula_checks.name: seniorDeductionFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Per-person6% phaseout is correct, but unknown MAGI gives an actual0 rather than a missing eligibility result.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Keep MAGI unknown distinct from a fully phased-out deduction; disclose conditional estimate.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: The per-person phase-out is right (C03, C04 and 10 of 10 senior witnesses agree). The unknown-income branch is never reached: no caller sends null (tax.ts:308, planning/index.ts:66). RECORDS FIX, file and code disagree: the hand-read formula in Calculation Module code/scripts/moneykeel_code_formula.py:506, printed into the tax.ts header (lines 192–195) and the master file's functions_from_code, still reads "full = people × $6,000; the answer = max(0, full − 6% × …)" — the couple-wide phase-out replaced on 2026-10-23 — while the code (tax.ts:229–231) and the package card are per person.
governing: IRS Schedule 1-A Part V; DEC-0240; DEC-0325

formula_checks.name: deductionFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Correct statutory amounts on an eligible standard-deduction return; MAGI/eligibility missing and nonstandard filing constraints are not represented.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Declare standard-deduction model scope, provide MAGI for senior phaseout and preserve unknown eligibility.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Code right on its domain (C01–C04 and 9 of 9 standard-deduction witnesses agree). The standard-deduction-only model is his DEC-0184 scope and every calculated rate says so on screen ("assuming the standard deduction", rateInForce covers, tax-rate.ts:170); MAGI is always handed in by the callers. Records fix only: the card's rule text should state that scope.

formula_checks.name: taxableIncomeFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Uses gross as MAGI; equivalent only when the caller has already adjusted gross to the statutory MAGI basis. Broad gross income can overphase the senior deduction.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Pass a distinct adjusted-income/MAGI value or explicitly constrain the model domain; do not phase the senior amount on unadjusted gross.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Code right for what callers send: every Cash flow caller hands it the income after the pre-tax 401(k) (taxedAfterPreTax; incomeSummary taxedOn), so C05 agrees through the real caller. Records fix: the rule text should say "gross" is the income after the 401(k), which the caller takes off. Real gap upstream, not here: the income handed in counts Social Security in full (part 17, MK-CF-F-084 APP WRONG), which also over-phases the senior deduction. Also seen: RetirementCockpit.tsx:221 hands marginalBracketFor the total gross before the 401(k) (Plan module, outside the next build's scope).

formula_checks.name: taxOwedFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Correct2026 band-by-band standard-deduction-model tax, plus the explicitly user-entered flat state assumption on taxable income. Full-return tax treatments and MAGI domain remain outside this primitive.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: All five of its cases agree with the reviewer to full precision.

formula_checks.name: effectiveRateOnGrossFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Divides the same modeled tax by its matching positive gross base; zero-income output is a rate sentinel, not proof of an entered0 tax rate.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: All five of its cases agree with the reviewer to full precision.

formula_checks.name: marginalBracketFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Correct inclusive upper-bound marginal band lookup on the modeled ordinary taxable income; zero taxable income maps to first band by convention, not a positive tax bill.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: All five of its cases agree with the reviewer to full precision.

formula_checks.name: ltcgRateFor
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Constants are correct, but one marginal rate selected from current ordinary income cannot price a finite gain that crosses the0/15/20% bands.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Label marginal baseline rate only; for tax on a gain, stack the gain over ordinary taxable income and slice it across bands.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: ltcgRateFor is a correct, labelled marginal lookup (C01, C02, C05 and 16 of 16 threshold witnesses agree). It has ONE caller and that caller misuses it: DrawSteerSheet.tsx:72 hands its rate to MK-PL-F-010 drawOrderOutcome, which taxes every dollar of gain drawn at it — single $48,111.17 ordinary taxable + a $3,311.43 gain: $0, right $295.89; joint $611,111.17 + $7,311.43: $1,096.71, right $1,332.84. RECORDS FIX too: its header says "Called by nothing" (tax.ts, after MK-CF-F-091 was retired) — the header builder does not see component callers.
formula_checks.fixed: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-TAX) — the caller stacks the gain (ltcgTaxOnGain); F-104 stays a labelled marginal lookup.

formula_checks.name: needsTakeHomeConversion
formula_checks.reviewer_why: Detects only a positive legacy take-home-mode record, without re-running conversion on already migrated data.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: All five of its cases agree with the reviewer to full precision.

formula_checks.name: convertTakeHomeMode
formula_checks.reviewer_why: The calculated-rate conversion inverts net to gross without adding back401(k) contributions, so the later gross−tax−401(k) cannot equal the typed take-home. Manual-rate branch handles401(k), calculated branch does not.
formula_checks.reviewer_should_be: Solve gross−pre-tax contributions−tax(gross−pre-tax contributions)=entered net; store a labeled estimate once.
formula_checks.what_the_code_actually_does: Real: the calculated branch omits the 401(k) from the inverse (take-home-mode-migration.ts:108). $4,211.17 a month typed, $511.43 401(k): gross $54,947.77, right $61,084.93; the converted profile then reads "your figures, 0%". The typed-rate branch (DEC-7942) is right (C01, C03 agree).
formula_checks.fixed_2026_10_25: FIXED 2026-10-25 (FIX-INCOME-A, landed 2026-10-26): gross − 401(k) − tax(gross − 401(k)) = the take-home entered, in both branches.
